ΔH ≈ Σ(bonds broken) − Σ(bonds made); gases only.
Energy needed to break one mole of a given covalent bond in gaseous molecules.
Exact: one bond in one molecule (H–H, Cl–Cl). Average: mean over many compounds (C–H, C–C).

front: Why bond-energy ΔH values are approximate
back: Average bond energies are used, and substances that are liquids or solids in standard states are treated as gases.

front: Finding ΔH for CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
back: Measure ΔH of CaCO₃ + acid and of CaO + acid; ΔH = ΔH₁ − ΔH₂.

front: ΔHc of graphite and ΔHf of CO₂
back: The same reaction, C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g), so the same value.
